cases.purpose: moves to /var/tmp (a different tmpfs, rename gives EXDEV) and back: a directory tree with nested data, a hardlinked pair and a symlink, a single file and a symlink keep bytes, modes, mtimes and hardlink topology and the sources disappear; an existing non-empty destination directory and an unwritable destination fail
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 mv(1) on the reference side, same guest and per-side mounts
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and the case tree: each invocation is bracketed by "[label]" markers on both streams and followed by its exit status; trusted python3 observers (fsobs.py) print metadata the tree snapshot does not hold. No normalisation. fsobs.py tree prints mode, mtime_ns, nlink and hardlink groups of the moved entries and of what remains in /var/tmp (the tree snapshot covers only the case directory and has no mtimes). r2 of the executed case (filesystem-45): setup now gives every entry the observer prints a fixed mtime, so mtime_ns lines compare preservation instead of the setup clock; steps unchanged.
cases.setup_script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
mkdir -p d/sub e /var/tmp/t/e /var/tmp/ro
printf 'x\0y' >d/sub/f
ln d/sub/f d/h
ln -s sub/f d/l
: >e/y
: >/var/tmp/t/e/x
printf one >f1
ln -s f1 s1
printf z >f2
/usr/bin/touch -h -d @1000000000 d/sub/f d/l d/sub
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000100 d
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000200 f1
/usr/bin/touch -h -d @1000000300 s1
chmod 750 d
chmod 640 d/sub/f
chmod 555 /var/tmp/ro
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000400 e/y /var/tmp/t/e/x f2
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000500 e /var/tmp/t/e
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000600 /var/tmp/t /var/tmp/ro
cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
r() { local label=$1; shift; echo "[$label]"; echo "[$label]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[$label] status=$?"; }
r dir-out mv d /var/tmp/d
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py tree /var/tmp/d d
r dir-back mv /var/tmp/d back
r file-out mv f1 /var/tmp/f1
r file-back mv /var/tmp/f1 f1back
r link-out mv s1 /var/tmp/s1
r link-back mv /var/tmp/s1 s1back
r nonempty-dest mv e /var/tmp/t
r unwritable-dest mv f2 /var/tmp/ro/
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py tree back f1back s1back e f2 d f1 s1
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py tree /var/tmp/t /var/tmp/ro /var/tmp/d /var/tmp/f1 /var/tmp/s1
/usr/bin/chmod 755 /var/tmp/ro

cases.purpose: link(2) from the case tmpfs to /var/tmp and /dev/shm, and from /var/tmp into the case tree, fails with EXDEV; no destination name appears and the sources keep one link
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 link(1) on the reference side, same guest and per-side mounts
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and the case tree: each invocation is bracketed by "[label]" markers on both streams and followed by its exit status; trusted python3 observers (fsobs.py) print metadata the tree snapshot does not hold. No normalisation. r2 of the executed case (filesystem-45): setup now gives every entry the observer prints a fixed mtime, so mtime_ns lines compare preservation instead of the setup clock; steps unchanged.
cases.setup_script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
printf payload >src
printf s >/var/tmp/s
/usr/bin/touch -d @1000000700 src /var/tmp/s
cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
r() { local label=$1; shift; echo "[$label]"; echo "[$label]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[$label] status=$?"; }
r to-var-tmp link src /var/tmp/alias
r to-dev-shm link src /dev/shm/alias
r into-case link /var/tmp/s dst
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py exists /var/tmp/alias /dev/shm/alias dst
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py tree src /var/tmp/s

cases.purpose: reading a directory fails with EISDIR on every block: with conv=noerror,sync each failed block is diagnosed, replaced by NUL padding and counted until count= is reached, with a nonzero final status; noerror without sync writes nothing for failed blocks; without noerror dd stops at the first error
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 dd(1) on the reference side, same guest and per-side mounts
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and the case tree: each invocation is bracketed by "[label]" markers on both streams and followed by its exit status; trusted python3 observers (fsobs.py) print metadata the tree snapshot does not hold. No normalisation. EISDIR from read(2) on a directory descriptor is a deterministic real kernel error. Each dd runs in a fresh shell under timeout(1) (status 124 on expiry): loadables/dd.c continues after a read error without counting the block, so the candidate is source-predicted to loop until the timeout. The single mid-stream EIO (r4) needs a sequenced seccomp reply and is not claimed here. r2 of the executed case (filesystem-45): the statistics step uses status=noxfer, so GNU prints the error and "records in/out" lines but not the elapsed-time/rate line, which cannot be byte-stable; other steps unchanged.
cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
r() { local label=$1; shift; echo "[$label]"; echo "[$label]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[$label] status=$?"; }
r noerror-sync /usr/bin/timeout 8 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'dd if=sub of=out1 bs=4 count=2 conv=noerror,sync status=none'
r noerror /usr/bin/timeout 8 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'dd if=sub of=out2 bs=4 count=2 conv=noerror status=none'
r noerror-stats /usr/bin/timeout 8 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'dd if=sub of=out3 bs=4 count=2 conv=noerror,sync status=noxfer'
r plain /usr/bin/timeout 8 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'dd if=sub of=out4 bs=4 count=2 status=none'
/usr/bin/python3 fsobs.py bytes out1 out2 out3 out4
/usr/bin/rm -f out1 out2 out3 out4
